span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SAME OBJECT HAS A NAME IN ANOTHER FIELD, AND THE PAPER SUPPLIES THE TRANSLATION: the functional's first variation formula CAN BE FOUND IN THE LITERATURE ON THE STRING THEORY, WHERE IT DESCRIBES THE LOW ENERGY EFFECTIVE ACTION - and THE FUNCTION f IS CALLED DILATON FIELD there. One mathematical object, two literatures, two names, and a citation offered so the reader can cross between them
span.note: about this quote: The span begins mid-sentence, at "and its first variation formula", because everything before it in that sentence is interleaved mathematics - "can be found in [H 4, § psi = (delta m)2 psi ... M gijRm R and its first variation formula". So the quote does not name WHICH functional, and the tag does not claim to. The translation it records - the same object called `dilaton field` in the string theory literature - is intact.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A MATHEMATICAL FREEDOM IS EXPLAINED BY A PHYSICS TERM RATHER THAN A MATHEMATICAL ONE: THE REMARKABLE FACT HERE IS THAT DIFFERENT CHOICES lead to THE SAME FLOW, up to a diffeomorphism - THAT IS, THE CHOICE OF m IS ANALOGOUS TO THE CHOICE OF GAUGE. The invariance is named by importing a word from another discipline, and the import is what makes it recognisable
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE ANALOGY'S STATUS IS MARKED AS HEURISTIC IN ITS OWN NUMBERED REMARK, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS SPELLED OUT: HEURISTICALLY, this statistical analogy IS RELATED TO the description of the renormalization group flow - IN THE LATTER one obtains quantities BY AVERAGING OVER HIGHER ENERGY STATES, WHEREAS IN THE FORMER THOSE STATES ARE SUPPRESSED by the exponential factor. The resemblance is asserted and the point of divergence given in the same breath
span.note: about this quote: CONTEXT THIS QUOTE CANNOT CARRY, recorded because it is the paper's central terminological hedge. The sentence that states the analogy is SCRAMBLED in the staged text and cannot be quoted: "In this section we show that the functional a sense analogous to minus entropy. W , introduced in section 3, is in" - the clean reading is "the functional W, introduced in section 3, is in a sense analogous to minus entropy". Damage shape 5. **The TITLE of the paper says `the entropy formula`; section 5 says `in a sense analogous to MINUS entropy` - qualified twice, by the hedge and by the sign - and that sentence is the one the extraction destroyed.**
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROPERTY IS DISCOVERED AND IMMEDIATELY GIVEN A NAME BUILT FROM TWO OTHER NAMES: a REMARKABLE PROPERTY of solutions with nonnegative curvature operator IN ARBITRARY DIMENSION is CALLED A DIFFERENTIAL HARNACK INEQUALITY, and what it ALLOWS is stated in the same sentence - comparing the curvatures at different points and different times. The name records neither the property nor its use but its lineage
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A RESULT IS VALUED BY WHAT IT UNBLOCKS IN SOMEONE ELSE'S PROGRAMME: the theorem is said to REMOVE THE MAJOR STUMBLING BLOCK IN HAMILTON'S APPROACH TO GEOMETRIZATION. The contribution is located relative to another person's plan rather than stated on its own terms
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A QUESTION IS PROPOSED AND CALLED NATURAL, WHICH IS THE ONLY WARRANT OFFERED FOR IT: Quotation withheld The word NATURAL carries the whole justification for why this is the question to ask next, and no other reason is given
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A TERM IS ATTRIBUTED TO A PERSON RATHER THAN DEFINED: a solution defined on a time interval of a certain form is ANCIENT, IN HAMILTON'S TERMINOLOGY - and the attribution is the definition's provenance, given in place of a criterion

span.label: The author could not establish Hamilton's expected boundedness of normalized curvature for eternal solutions.
span.note: what this limits: the eternal-solutions claim: WE HAVE NOT BEEN ABLE TO CONFIRM HAMILTON'S HOPE THAT THE SOLUTION THAT EXISTS FOR ALL TIME NECESSARILY HAS BOUNDED NORMALIZED CURVATURE

span.label: No proof is given that the limiting construction yields a canonically defined Ricci flow through singularities.
span.note: what this limits: the canonical-flow-through-singularities claim: IT IS LIKELY THAT ... ONE WOULD GET A CANONICALLY DEFINED RICCI FLOW THROUGH SINGULARITIES, BUT AT THE MOMENT I DON'T HAVE A PROOF OF THAT

span.label: The author states his own understanding is insufficient for the physics analogy invoked (Black Hole Thermodynamics).
span.note: what this limits: the physical analogy only: UNFORTUNATELY, THIS SUBJECT IS BEYOND MY UNDERSTANDING AT THE MOMENT - the Black Hole Thermodynamics parallel is offered without being vouched for

span.label: The result the paper is famous for is presented as a brief sketch.

span.label: The curvature fact the blow-up analysis rests on is imported from earlier work and holds in dimension three.
span.note: what this limits: the nonnegative-curvature property of blow-up limits used here: it rests on results of Ivey and Hamilton proved in dimension three, where large scalar curvature makes the negative part of the curvature tensor comparatively small

span.note: what this limits: any comparison of this reduced-volume formula with Huisken's monotonicity formula for mean curvature flow: the author states the two resemble each other but that here the monotonicity runs in the opposite direction
